title: Things to know when you get cancer
title_zh: 患癌时需要注意的事项

paragraphs.en: I was diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma in my mouth in May 2026. Here are some things I learned based on that experience so far.
paragraphs.zh: 2026年5月，我被诊断出口腔鳞状细胞癌。 以下是我根据这段经历到目前为止学到的一些事情。

sents.en: I was diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma in my mouth in May 2026.
sents.zh: 2026年5月，我被诊断出口腔鳞状细胞癌。

sents.en: Here are some things I learned based on that experience so far.
sents.zh: 以下是我根据这段经历到目前为止学到的一些事情。

paragraphs.en: Note, since this is on the front page of Hacker News right now. exhilaration suggested that if you are within a 2-3 hour drive of a major cancer center, go there instead of your local community hospital. Use the US News cancer hospital rankings . The top centers usually take your insurance, so use vacation days and book a hotel if you have to. The largest benefit I saw was speed. At MD Anderson I got a question answered within 20 minutes of a visit, because the doctor called the pathologist who he was on a first name basis with. If that wasn’t at a cancer center, it would have taken days, or more likely the question never would have been answered at all (I had asked my oncologist about this and he’d just shrugged). The rest of the HN comments are worth reading too.
paragraphs.zh: 请注意，这条内容现在正位于 Hacker News 首页。exhilaration 建议，如果你距离某家大型癌症中心只有 2-3 小时车程，那就去那里，而不是去当地社区医院。 可以参考《美国新闻与世界报道》的癌症医院排名。 顶级癌症中心通常接受你的保险，所以必要时请使用年假并预订一家酒店。 我看到最大的好处是速度快。 在 MD Anderson，我访问后 20 分钟内就得到了问题的答案，因为那位医生给一位与他熟识、直呼其名的病理学家打了电话。 如果不是在癌症中心，这可能需要好几天，或者更可能的是这个问题根本就得不到解答（我曾就此问过我的肿瘤科医生，他只是耸了耸肩）。 HN 上的其余评论也值得一读。
